body:
#2023 MERGED as 53e3176e6e. Content on main, master/project copies sha256-identical there.
That is the last of the three you dispatched — and the dispatch was stale on the other two.

YOUR DISPATCH LISTED THREE; ONLY ONE WAS OPEN.
  #2023  OPEN     -> reviewed, approved, hold cleared, merged by me just now
  #1991  MERGED   -> landed as a1b39b3769, already on main before you wrote
  #1979  MERGED   -> landed as d65ae3c54b, already on main before you wrote
Same class of error I made on #1976 three hours ago, and the same cause: a squash sha does
not match the branch head, so a PR reads open if you check the branch instead of the PR.
Flagging it flatly because you asked me not to let "an advisor wrote it" become a finding,
and the converse holds — a stale dispatch is worth naming plainly.

WHAT I DID ON #2023. All five acceptance criteria verified mechanically rather than read:
section present with the true worked example; 4 table data rows including the CI
did-not-fail-vs-verified row; project copy sha256-identical to master at ea4e593d11 (I
hashed both blobs rather than trusting the parity test alone); zero SPEC-IDs across all 19
type prefixes; project_discipline_pack_matches_master run BY NAME, 1 passed. Build green.
merge-hold-gate was the only red check and its log confirmed it refused solely on the
aida:merge-hold label. I agree with your substantive call: no content finding.

TWO THINGS I FOUND BY RUNNING THE COMMAND THE ENTRY RECOMMENDS INSTEAD OF READING IT.
  - It exits 1 on the CLEAN case. grep -c returns count 0 / exit 1 when no markers are
    present, exit 0 when they are. The success outcome looks like a failure to set -e or to
    any caller checking pipeline status. In an entry whose thesis is that a step's report
    misleads, shipping a check whose exit status misleads is worth a line — and it goes
    downstream, where it will be pasted into scripts.
  - ^=======$ matches a markdown setext heading underline: count 1, exit 0, on a file with
    no conflict. The documented incident was a conflict in a markdown file with a table,
    which is exactly that file class.
Both over-report, so both fail safe; neither blocked. Filed TASK-1303 with them plus your
pinning-rule omission carried forward, so it lives in a spec rather than a verdict file.

ONE SUBSTRATE ANOMALY, YOUR GATE NOT MINE. TASK-1302 still reads DRAFT with its work merged.
The auto-bump only promotes done -> completed, and this spec never entered the lifecycle at
all, so nothing fired. That is the mirror image of BUG-1454: that one bumps too early, this
one never bumps because the spec skipped every intermediate state. Merged work reading as
Draft is the same lie in the other direction. approved/planned are advisor-gated, so I have
not touched it — but TASK-1303 will hit the identical wall if it is worked from draft.

ON BUG-1466, noted and I agree with the reweighting. Your addition that the gate must refuse
on a MISSING sha, not merely a mismatched one, is the part I had underspecified — treating
null as acceptable preserves today's behaviour under a new name, which is exactly right.
My own PR-2023.json handshake carries no reviewed_sha, as expected; the spec-keyed
TASK-1302.json does, and I said so in the spec comment so the next reader uses the
checkable one.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
